limitations: The joint frontier is offline and assumes the same scenario weighting as E68-E71; production traffic prevalence can change the aggregate optimum.
Certification and drift geometric means are descriptive objectives, not a utility function. Operational selection should use an explicit worst-drift cap.
Worst-case ratios are checkpoint-quantized and can change discontinuously when a boundary crosses one scheduled look.
The 5% positive-weight grid excludes continuous optima and reserves alpha for every metric family.
Weights remain valid only when preregistered or selected from independent data; monitored outcomes cannot choose their own allocation without additional multiplicity control.
All earlier independence, expected-proportion, delayed-label, and checkpoint-only limitations remain.
model: Evaluate every E71 metric-alpha allocation as one preregistered global controller configuration. Join its E71 certification cost with fresh E70-style drift response for every active breach, then select allocations under explicit worst-case drift-slowdown caps.

validation.cap_feasibility: Each cap-selected allocation has maximum drift ratio no greater than the declared cap.
validation.equal_control: Equal alpha reproduces every finite E70 drift crossing exactly and is feasible under every cap.
validation.pareto_definition: An allocation is retained when no other allocation has no-larger certification and drift geometric means with at least one strict improvement.
